required_maintenance_order.action: Freeze the maintenance window and confirm the final security-safe preflight remains ROTATION BLOCKED.
required_maintenance_order.compatibility_rule: Do not begin execution while the protected-artifact baseline discrepancy is unresolved unless separately approved as an integrity exception.

required_maintenance_order.action: Block new submissions and scheduled producers, drain workers without interrupting active ingestion, and stop backend and worker credential consumers. If draining would touch the protected chapter or require recovery changes, postpone maintenance. Stage replacement secrets in an approved secure store without applying them yet.
required_maintenance_order.compatibility_rule: Assume a coordinated outage. Existing PostgreSQL roles and AIStor root identities do not have proven dual-password support. Do not create substitute roles or change privileges implicitly.

required_maintenance_order.action: Using an approved secure administrative session, change the existing PostgreSQL role password and synchronize its authoritative deployment source and all backend, worker and stopped one-shot client sources.
required_maintenance_order.compatibility_rule: Changing container initialization variables alone does not change an existing database role password. Keep consumers stopped; keep PostgreSQL available. Do not run migrations or change role ownership/grants.

required_maintenance_order.action: Verify replacement PostgreSQL authentication with isolated approved client checks before starting application traffic or workers.
required_maintenance_order.compatibility_rule: Do not execute migration entrypoints. Do not restart Redis. Keep normal clients quiesced for the AIStor cutover.

required_maintenance_order.action: Record only PostgreSQL authentication success booleans and verify old-password rejection through a secure isolated verifier.
required_maintenance_order.compatibility_rule: A role password change supersedes the old password immediately; it is not a later revocation step. Existing sessions may persist and must not be mistaken for successful new authentication.

required_maintenance_order.action: Stage replacement AIStor root credentials and matching S3 client sources, including the stopped storage-init definition, using the proven authoritative environment or file source.
required_maintenance_order.compatibility_rule: Do not assume root credential overlap. If precedence or the supported AIStor rotation procedure is unproven, stop execution. Do not run storage-init.

required_maintenance_order.action: Apply the supported AIStor root credential cutover and perform only the necessary AIStor restart or recreation, preserving exact image, data volume, license mount, endpoints and bucket configuration.
required_maintenance_order.compatibility_rule: Keep backend and worker stopped until AIStor accepts the replacement. Never remove volumes or recreate storage data; do not upgrade the image or rotate the license.

required_maintenance_order.action: Verify AIStor replacement authentication and old-credential rejection with approved metadata-only operations, then start backend with ingress blocked and verify PostgreSQL and S3. Verify the worker configuration using an isolated non-consuming authentication check before starting its consumer process.
required_maintenance_order.compatibility_rule: Do not run storage-init, create/delete buckets, alter policies, run migrations, or access chapter/object contents.

required_maintenance_order.action: Resume worker consumers, then scheduled producers and ingress only after both credential systems pass. Retire rollback secret-store versions according to approved retention after the observation window.
required_maintenance_order.compatibility_rule: Root replacement supersedes old credentials at cutover, not at a fictional later revoke step. Keep the affected chapter excluded from scheduling; if exclusion requires ingestion/recovery changes, postpone execution.

pre_rotation_safety_checks: Confirm final preflight artifact and sidecars are preserved.
Confirm decision remains ROTATION BLOCKED and no readiness override exists.
Reconcile the protected-artifact baseline discrepancy as a separate integrity item; do not overwrite the baseline.
Confirm target service identities, Compose project identity, image identities, endpoint identities, bucket identity, and credential fingerprints are recorded only as approved non-secret metadata.
Confirm maintenance owner, rollback owner, approval, maintenance window, and secret-store version identifiers are recorded without values.
Confirm no AIStor license rotation is in scope.
Confirm existing object namespace and affected chapter identifier are protected from write, delete, read, or validation activity.
Confirm no migration, storage-init mutation, ingestion/recovery change, or Redis restart is scheduled.

rollback.principle: Use secret-store version rollback or an approved credential reactivation procedure; never write old values to logs, artifacts, command lines, or chat.
trigger_conditions: Any required authenticated boolean check fails
Backend or worker cannot initialize with the replacement credential
Unexpected object, chapter, policy, endpoint, or application behavior is detected
Integrity discrepancy is not separately acknowledged and controlled
order: Keep ingress and workers paused. For PostgreSQL, restore the prior role password through the approved secure administrative channel and restore matching secret-store source versions; reverting environment variables alone is insufficient.

For AIStor, restore the prior authoritative root secret-store source version and perform the supported server restart or recreation with unchanged data volume and license mount. Restore matching client sources before restarting clients.
Restart or recreate only the affected authorized clients.

Record only opaque version IDs, timestamps, component names, and boolean outcomes. Resume traffic only after compatibility is verified. If prior credentials cannot safely be reactivated, remain offline and use an approved forward-fix credential rather than exposing old values.

data_protection.object_operations: No list, get, put, delete, policy mutation, or storage initialization operation is part of this plan.

post_rotation_verification.output_policy: Authenticated success/failure booleans only; no values, tokens, URLs containing credentials, environment dumps, or object contents.
postgresql: required one-shot client authenticated: boolean, if applicable
